title: Generated event logs: is the stated count of events correct for this log?
decision: whether a claim about the number of events of one service and level in a time window is correct for the given log (yes) or not (no)

source.name: generator build/gen_log_count_check.py
source.version: gen_v4, 2026-10-08: stated counts equally distributed in both classes within every level (no zero-claim cue), number agreement in the claim wording, meta.level = 1/2/3 and meta.log_level

licence: generated by the benchmark's script (no third-party text)
notes: 600 items = 300 contrast pairs (meta.pair, group): one log with a true claim (yes) and the same log with the claim changed in one field (no): stated count off by one or two, the window replaced by the neighbouring window, or the service replaced by another service of the log (the stated count is then that of the window / service of the pair's true claim). The metric is item accuracy; the group allows a pair analysis. Dial: lines (30, 60, 90) = meta.level 1, 2, 3; meta.log_level is the severity named in the claim. Within every level the stated counts of the negatives and the true counts of the positives have the same histogram (0 to 4, 0 to 8, 0 to 12; L1 distance 2 per level, the minimum), so a claim of 0 events is as often true as false and no table 'stated count -> answer' beats chance. The noun after the count agrees with it ('1 ERROR event'). Everything is invented and every answer is computed twice (specification and a parser of the rendered text). gen_v4 (2026-10-08) fixes: stated counts equal per level, singular / plural agreement, meta.level = difficulty level and meta.log_level = claim severity. State length 1114 to 3659 characters (median 2208).

sample.note: a sample of two whole contrast groups (one of level 1, one of level 3) for the tests of this repository; EVALUATION ONLY, never a training source
